'''Ambrogio Fasoli''' (born 10 November 1964 in Milan) is a researcher and professor working in the field of [[Nuclear fusion|fusion]] and [[Plasma (physics)#Research|plasma physics]]. Since January 2025, he is Vice President for Academic Affairs at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne]] (EPFL).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Vice Presidencies |url=https://www.epfl.ch/about/vice-presidencies/ |access-date=2025-01-07 |website=EPFL |language=en-GB}}</ref> He was Associate Vice President for Research at EPFL since 2021.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Rauss |first=Frédéric |date=2020-11-12 |title=The new Vice Presidency for Academic Affairs (VPA) |url=https://actu.epfl.ch/news/the-new-vice-presidency-for-academic-affairs-vpa-6/ |access-date=2021-05-18 |website=EPFL, Ecole Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne}}</ref>

A Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]], he is Director of the Swiss Plasma Center, located at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL]]. Since 1 January 2019, he chairs the European consortium [[EUROfusion]], the umbrella organisation for the development of nuclear fusion power in Europe.<ref>{{Cite web|last=EUROfusion|title=Interview Jérôme Paméla and Ambrogio Fasoli|url=https://www.euro-fusion.org/news/2019/january/interview-jerome-pamela-and-ambrogio-fasoli/|access-date=2021-05-18|website=www.euro-fusion.org|language=en}}</ref>

From 2014 through 2020, he was also Editor-in-Chief of [[Nuclear Fusion (journal)|''Nuclear Fusion'']],<ref>{{Cite web|title=New Editor-in-Chief for Nuclear Fusion|url=https://iopscience.iop.org/journal/0029-5515/page/New-Editor-in-Chief-for-Nuclear-Fusion|access-date=2021-05-26|website=Nuclear Fusion - IOPscience}}</ref> the peer-reviewed [[scientific journal]] of the [[International Atomic Energy Agency]] (IAEA). Fasoli represents Switzerland on the Governing Board of [[Fusion for Energy|Fusion For Energy]], the agency that manages Europe's contributions to the international fusion reactor project [[ITER]].

== Career ==
Fasoli graduated from [[University of Milan|the University of Milan]], (in physics, 1988) and from [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL, the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Lausanne]] (PhD in Science, 1993, EPFL best thesis award). He went on to do his post-doctoral research on [[Joint European Torus|JET]], the world's largest fusion reactor, participating in 1997 in the experiments that still hold the record for fusion power generated for peaceful purposes by a plasma on earth.

He joined the Physics Department of the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT) as tenure track assistant professor in 1997. At MIT, he led the plasma physics research group and coordinated the international scientific collaboration between MIT and JET.

In 2001, he joined the EPFL Faculty of Basic Sciences, then became associate professor, before being appointed full professor in physics in 2008. In 2007, he was appointed executive director of the Centre de Recherches en Physique des Plasmas (CRPP), of which he became director in 2013, and which became the Swiss Plasma Center in 2015<ref>{{Cite news|date=2015-09-22|title=Production d'énergie: entretien avec Ambrogio Fasoli, directeur du Swiss Plasma Center sur le site de l'EPFL|work=Radio Télévision Suisse (RTS)|url=https://www.rts.ch/play/tv/12h45/video/production-denergie-entretien-avec-ambrogio-fasoli-directeur-du-swiss-plasma-center-sur-le-site-de-lepfl?urn=urn:rts:video:7106093|access-date=2021-05-20}}</ref> Fasoli was responsible for several years for EPFL's [[Tokamak à configuration variable|TCV Tokamak]], one of the national facilities in Europe participating in the research for the international reactor ITER<ref>{{Cite web|date=2015-09-28|title=Swiss Plasma Center: a new name for a strengthened role|url=https://www.iter.org/newsline/-/2284|access-date=2021-05-20|website=ITER}}</ref>

In 2008, Fasoli was elected as a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=American Physical Society fellow archive|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?year=|access-date=2021-05-20|website=American Physical Society}}</ref> Since 2001, he has been a visiting professor in the Department of Physics at MIT<ref>{{Cite web|title=Alfvén Wave Instabilities – a collaboration between PSFC and JET|url=https://www1.psfc.mit.edu/research/physics_research/plasma_diagnostics_new/alven.html|access-date=2021-05-20|website=Plasma Science and Fusion Center, Massachusetts Institute of Technology}}</ref>

From 2010 through 2014, he was the Head of Physics Strategic Committee, and a member of the Directorate of the EPFL Basic Science Faculty. Since 1 January 2019, he is the chair of the European consortium [[EUROfusion]], the umbrella organization of Europe's fusion laboratories.

He has developed a [[Massive open online course|Massive open online course (MOOC)]] dedicated to fusion and plasma physics, with several thousand registrations each year.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Plasma Physics: introduction|url=https://www.edx.org/course/plasma-physics-introduction|access-date=2021-05-20|website=edX, the American massive open online course (MOOC) provider created by Harvard and MIT}}</ref>

=== Scientific contributions ===
Fasoli works in the areas of basic [[Plasma (physics)|plasma physics]], [[burning plasma]] physics, and [[Tokamak|tokamak physics]]. At the Swiss Plasma Center, located at EPFL (the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Lausanne), he has founded and led the basic plasmas research group, and built the TORPEX facility.<ref>{{Cite web|title=The TORPEX device|url=https://www.epfl.ch/research/domains/swiss-plasma-center/research/research_basic_plasmas/research_basic_plasmas_torpex/|access-date=2021-05-25|website=www.epfl.ch|language=en-GB}}</ref> He was responsible for the [[Tokamak à configuration variable|TCV tokamak]], the experimental fusion reactor, for several years.
<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Fasoli, Ambrogio; Furno, Ivo; Ricci, Paolo|date=2019|title=The role of basic plasmas studies in the quest for fusion power|journal=Nature Physics|volume=15|issue=9|pages=872–875|doi=10.1038/s41567-019-0622-5|bibcode=2019NatPh..15..872F|s2cid=199435782}}</ref> plasma physics and nuclear fusion.

At MIT, (1997-2001), he founded and led the plasma physics research group, constructing the [[Versatile Toroidal Facility]] (VTF) experiment to study the physics of [[magnetic reconnection]], and coordinated the international scientific collaboration between MIT and JET.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Alfvén wave instabilities - a collaboration between PSFC and JET|url=https://www1.psfc.mit.edu/research/physics_research/plasma_diagnostics_new/alven.html|access-date=2021-05-25|website=MIT Plasma Science and Fusion Center}}</ref>

As a researcher at JET, he initiated a series of experiments on the interaction between plasma particles and [[Alfvén wave]]s, of interest to fusion reactor plasmas. He participated in 1997 in the experiments that still hold the record for fusion power generated for peaceful purposes by a plasma on earth<ref>{{Cite news|date=2014-04-24|title=JET experiment aims to reach breakeven point in nuclear fusion|journal=Physics Today|doi=10.1063/PT.5.027874|url=https://physicstoday.scitation.org/do/10.1063/PT.5.027874/full/|access-date=2021-05-25}}</ref>

== Awards and honours ==

* Polysphère, EPFL (the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology) best teacher's award (2008 and 2014)
* Fellow of American Physical Society (2008)
* [[Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions|Marie Curie Fellowship]], as host of Dr. P.Ricci (2006)
* Marie Curie Fellowship, as host of Dr. M.McGrath (2002)
* [[Swiss National Science Foundation]] Professeur Boursier (2001)
* [[United States Department of Energy|US Department of Energy]] - Plasma Physics Junior Faculty Award (2000)
* MIT Charles Reed Faculty Award (1999)
* EPFL best thesis Award (1993)
